title: add transactional downgrade guard, version pinning, and backup/restore improvements to private installer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: This PR implements transactional schema migrations, a downgrade guard for upgrade/rollback operations, stronger version-pinning for Helm and Terraform artifacts used by the private installer, and improvements to backup/restore verification used during upgrades. Motivation: recent upgrade incidents exposed two failure modes: partially-applied schema migrations that prevented rollback, and unclear interaction between chart/module version drift and the rollback tooling. This PR aims to make upgrades atomic (or strongly reversible), add guards to prevent unsafe downgrades, and improve the pre-upgrade backup/restore verification flow so rollbacks are reliable.

What changed (high level):
- transactional migration wrapper: migrations are applied in a transactional wrapper that records an ordered migration manifest and either commits all steps or provides an automated rollback path when supported by the DB.
- downgrade guard: installer now verifies version compatibility and rejects/aborts automatic downgrades unless a forced path is used and an explicit restore plan exists.
- version pinning: Helm Chart.yaml and internal Terraform module references are pinned to tested commit SHAs / chart versions during release builds to avoid implicit drift during in-place upgrades.
- backup/restore verification: added end-to-end restore verification that performs a dry-run restore into an ephemeral namespace/cluster and validates key invariants (schema version, KV counts, service account integrity).
- rollback tooling: improved orchestration script for rollback that coordinates helm rollback, DB restore, and KV cache invalidation with better logging and failure handling.
- docs & tests: upgrade-guide updated with the new pre-upgrade checklist and a new CI job that runs the e2e upgrade/rollback scenario in a dedicated pipeline.

Why this approach: making migrations transactional reduces blast radius and ensures we have an automated path out of partial upgrades. Version pinning prevents surprises from transitive dependency updates during a tenant upgrade. The downgrade guard enforces explicit intent for unsafe operations and surfaces required manual steps for irreversible changes.

Testing & validation:
- unit tests for migration wrapper and version-check logic added (see tests/upgrade).
- CI: new pipeline ci/upgrade-e2e.yaml runs an upgrade from vX.Y.Z -> vX.Y.Z+1 and a rollback path to verify restore succeeds end-to-end.
- Ran a staged rollout in our internal lab cluster against 3 private-installer deployments and verified successful rollback in simulated failure injection scenarios.

Rollout plan: merge to main, include in next private-installer release candidate. For existing customers we will ship as opt-in by default for the first week while we monitor the upgrade-e2e job and logs; full-enforcement of the downgrade guard will be enabled 2 weeks after the release if no regressions are observed.

Related: Linear ENG-2314 (transactional migrations), ENG-2390 (upgrade safety), ENG-2456 (backup/restore verification). SUP-456 documents a customer incident that motivated this change.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] e2e upgrade/rollback CI job added
- [x] Docs updated (docs/upgrade.md)
- [x] Helm and Terraform pinning in CI changes
- [x] Rollout plan stated
commits_summary: feat(migrations): add transactional migration wrapper and manifest tracking; feat(downgrade-guard): implement safety checks and explicit force path; chore(helm): pin chart versions in release job; feat(backup): add restore verification dry-run and invariants check; feat(rollback): improve orchestration script with retries and cache invalidation; docs: update upgrade guide and release notes; test: add e2e upgrade/rollback pipeline
files_changed_summary: charts/private-installer/Chart.yaml (version pinning and annotations); charts/private-installer/values.yaml (defaults for safe-upgrade flags); installer/upgrade/transactional_migrations.go (new transactional wrapper and manifest storage); installer/upgrade/rollback_tooling.sh (orchestration & improved logging); installer/backup/restore_verify.go (dry-run restore & invariants); terraform/modules/private_installer/main.tf (module source pinning + version variables); ci/upgrade-e2e.yaml (new pipeline); tests/e2e/upgrade_rollback.test.ts; docs/upgrade.md; scripts/release/pin-helm-versions.sh; charts/templates/NOTES.txt (upgrade notes); .github/workflows/upgrade-e2e.yml
review_comments: Maya Chen (requested changes): Can you add a timeout and backoff for the migration manifest write? In large clusters we've seen the storage write stall and that caused our previous incident. Also please surface a clear pre-flight check error code so CLI/CI can detect and fail early.

Asha Patel (author reply): Added a bounded retry with exponential backoff to the manifest writer and returned explicit exit codes for pre-flight failures. See installer/upgrade/transactional_migrations.go lines ~120-180.

Diego Ramos (comment): We need unit tests for the DB rollback path that simulate a failed mid-migration step and verify manifest-driven rollback executes. Please add table-driven tests covering Postgres transaction failure and partial-apply scenarios.

Asha Patel (author reply): Added tests in tests/upgrade/migrations_test.go that cover failed-step rollback and manifest-driven recovery. Tests mock the DB driver to simulate a mid-transaction failure.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified CI e2e run and lab rollout. Small nits about log levels fixed. Approve once CI green.
CI Bot: ci/upgrade-e2e completed (pass). Helm lint and terraform validate passed. Security SBOM check passed.
release_notes:
- Add transactional schema migration wrapper to make upgrades atomic or recoverable.
- Add downgrade guard to prevent unsafe automatic downgrades; requires explicit force flag and documented restore path.
- Pin Helm chart and Terraform module versions during release to avoid drift during in-place upgrades.
- Add backup/restore dry-run verification used as a pre-upgrade gate.
- Improve rollback orchestration with better logging, retries, and cache invalidation.
notes: This PR is focused on making private-installer upgrades safer; customers on Dedicated/Private should test the RC in staging before scheduling production upgrades.
